title: DBLab vs Vela: clones of any Postgres vs branches on Vela
description: Vela is a self-hosted Postgres platform that branches its own databases with copy-on-write NVMe storage. DBLab clones any PostgreSQL where it already runs.
summary: Vela, from simplyblock, is a self-hostable Postgres platform built from a fork of Supabase Studio and simplyblock's NVMe storage. Branches and clones of a Vela database are copy-on-write at the block level, and each runs as its own instance. Existing databases are loaded into Vela with pg_dump and psql. simplyblock announced the public beta in February 2026. DBLab Engine is open-source software that makes thin clones of any PostgreSQL, including managed services, without moving it. Pick Vela if you want to run your Postgres on a self-hosted platform with branching built in; pick DBLab to clone databases that stay where they are.
chooseThem: Branching is built into the platform your databases run on, in your own infrastructure, with block-level copy-on-write that Vela says forks 1TB in under a second at the storage layer.
A full Postgres platform, not only copies: Vela Studio, RBAC, scheduled backups with point-in-time restore, and separate scaling of compute and storage.
Each branch is a separate database instance with its own resource limits, so tests on one branch run on their own compute.
The code is open source under Apache 2.0 or MIT.
A free hosted sandbox with 2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM and 100 GiB NVMe to try it before self-hosting.

rows.them: A self-hostable, serverless Postgres development platform with database branching and separate scaling of compute and storage. It combines a fork of Supabase Studio, a controller and simplyblock storage.

Branches and clones are made from branches in a Vela project. Existing data is loaded with pg_dump and psql for Postgres-to-Postgres moves, or with CSV and pgloader imports; the sources we reviewed do not describe ongoing sync from an external database.
Copy-on-write at the block level in simplyblock's distributed NVMe storage. A fork or snapshot is a metadata-only operation; a VM is then provisioned and the volume attached.

Vela says forking a 1TB database typically completes in under one second at the storage layer and that clone time is independent of data size. The clone guide says it "may take a few moments"; a new database usually takes less than a minute.
Cloning a branch copies the schema, data and configuration into a new, independent branch. Branches can also start from a snapshot, and scheduled backups allow point-in-time restore.
Not documented in the sources we reviewed.

Vela describes a pipeline that creates a branch for a pull request, runs tests and migrations, then deletes it. The sources we reviewed include no CI integration, API or CLI reference for that workflow.

Vela Studio, a web dashboard, for projects, branches and clones. Vela's branching page says branches can be created from the UI or an API; the sources we reviewed do not include an API, CLI or MCP reference for branch operations.
Self-hosted on Kubernetes, OpenShift, bare metal or VMs, on AWS, GCP, Azure or on-premises. simplyblock announced the public beta on February 9, 2026. A free hosted sandbox is offered for evaluation.
"All code is either Apache License 2.0 or MIT licensed." The main simplyblock/vela repository is under Apache 2.0.

Sandbox: 2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM, 100 GiB NVMe and 10,000 IOPS; databases pause after inactivity and public internet transfer is blocked. The sources we reviewed do not state limits for self-hosted deployments.
Self-hosted Enterprise is licensed per vCPU, at a custom price that depends on deployment scope; compute and storage run on your own infrastructure. The sandbox is free.

pricing.notes: Hosted, for evaluation; 2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM, 100 GiB NVMe, 10,000 IOPS; branches and clones bound by these resources
Self-hosted on Kubernetes, OpenShift or private cloud; licensed per vCPU; priority support and rollout engineering

faq.a: Yes. simplyblock says all Vela code is under Apache 2.0 or MIT, and the main repository on GitHub is Apache 2.0. Enterprise support for self-hosted deployments is sold separately.

faq.q: Can Vela branch a database that runs on Amazon RDS?
faq.a: Not in place. Vela branches databases in a Vela project, so an existing database has to be loaded first; the docs recommend pg_dump and psql. DBLab clones such databases where they are, by dump and restore.

simplyblock announced the public beta of Vela on February 9, 2026. The product pages we read today do not say beta or generally available, and the open-source announcement calls the release a request for feedback.
The hosted sandbox is free. Self-hosted Enterprise is licensed per vCPU at a custom price; you also pay for your own compute and storage.

proofs.them: Vela branches and clones are made from branches in a Vela project. An existing PostgreSQL database is loaded into Vela first; Vela's docs recommend pg_dump and psql for Postgres-to-Postgres moves.

Each Vela branch is a separate database instance with its own resource limits. Self-hosted Enterprise is licensed per vCPU at a custom price that depends on deployment scope; the hosted sandbox is free.

Vela describes creating a branch per pull request from the UI or an API, then running migrations and tests on it. The sources we reviewed do not describe a check that fails a migration on lock duration.
